composio.note: Composio manages a Gmail OAuth app (default for prototypes). Create a custom auth config with your own client ID and secret for launch, and copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

need_own_app.answer: For prototypes, no: Composio's managed Gmail app works. For launch, yes if you want your own branding on the consent screen, scopes beyond Composio's defaults, or a dedicated quota.
reasons: Managed app shows 'Composio wants to access your account' instead of your brand
Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need
Managed apps share quota across all Composio users
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers
Your own app gets a dedicated quota

prerequisites.title: Public domain with home page and privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: Home page must be public and describe the app; the privacy policy must be on the same domain and disclose how Google user data is used. Domains must be verified in Google Search Console.

prerequisites.title: Google Cloud project
prerequisites.detail: Create the project and configure the consent screen under Google Auth platform > Branding. You must agree to the Google API Services User Data Policy.

steps.title: Create consent screen and choose user type
steps.detail: In Google Cloud console, configure Branding, pick Internal or External, and agree to the User Data Policy.

steps.title: Pick the narrowest Gmail scopes
steps.detail: Map each agent feature to the least-permissive scope and write a justification for each sensitive or restricted scope.
steps.done_when: Scope list and written justifications are ready.

steps.title: Verify domains and publish branding
steps.detail: Verify domain ownership in Search Console, then click Verify Branding and Publish branding.
inputs: Home page and privacy policy URLs

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Show the English OAuth grant flow, consent screen with app name and client ID in the address bar, and each scope's use. Upload to YouTube as Unlisted.

steps.title: Draft scope justifications and demo script
steps.detail: Write per-scope justifications, why narrower scopes won't work, and a video script.
steps.done_when: Text is ready to paste into the form.

steps.title: Submit for verification
steps.detail: Submit from the OAuth consent screen with justifications and video link.
steps.done_when: Request appears in the OAuth Verification Center.

steps.title: Wait for Google verification
steps.detail: Google may email for more information. Respond quickly.

steps.title: Complete security assessment if restricted
steps.detail: Required if you store or transmit restricted-scope data on servers.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a Composio auth config for gmail with your own client ID and secret, and add the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard to your Google OAuth client.
steps.done_when: Test user connects via your app.

traps.title: Apps in development or testing are still subject to
traps.detail: Apps in development or testing are still subject to a tester warning screen, a user cap, and a limited refresh token lifetime.

traps.title: Testing mode caps users and expires tokens
traps.detail: Testing apps allow only 100 test users and refresh tokens expire after 7 days. Do not launch to customers in Testing.

traps.title: Unverified published apps hit a 100-user cap
traps.detail: A published but unverified app requesting sensitive or restricted scopes shows warning screens and has a hard cap of 100 total users.

traps.title: Multiple OAuth clients multiply demo videos
traps.detail: A developer reported that each OAuth client in one project needs its own restricted-scope demo video. Delete clients not ready for production.

traps.title: Branding is locked during verification
traps.detail: Branding changes are not allowed while verification is in progress; cancel it first. Branding approvals expire after 7 days if unpublished.

traps.title: Callback domain cannot be verified by you
traps.detail: Google requires verification of domains tied to redirect URIs, but Composio's callback domain cannot be verified by the developer. Route the callback through your own domain via Composio's redirect proxy (302 redirect to Composio).

traps.title: Admins can block even verified apps
traps.detail: Verification does not override Workspace administrator settings.

blockers.symptom: Unverified app screen appears during testing
blockers.what_it_means: The app needs verification to remove the warning.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft justifications and a demo script.

blockers.what_it_means: Often the consent screen, demo or privacy policy does not match requirements, or the sign-in flow skips the Sign in with Google button.
blockers.what_to_do: Fix the issues and respond to Trust & Safety emails; recheck the demo against Google's checklist.
blockers.agent_can_help: Audit the demo script and branding fields against the checklist.

evidence.answer: Blocker reported by a developer (2019): multiple OAuth clients in one project each need restricted-scope demo videos, and missing ones cause repeated review rounds.

evidence.quote: This can result in delays or failure in verification.
evidence.answer: Common blocker: a sign-in flow that skips the 'Sign in with Google' button (for example, a login_hint without a prompt setting) can cause verification delays or failure.

evidence.quote: The “secure OAuth flows” warning is not an automatic rejection. It’s mainly a recommendation.
evidence.answer: Forum reply (unofficial, from a community member, not Google staff): the 'not configured to use secure OAuth flows' warning is not an automatic rejection, and PKCE is generally acceptable.
